text:
amanda.lee: heads-up — I ran into a weird production case where long-lived API keys (created years ago) are still being used by a handful of infra jobs. we need a migration/handoff plan to rotate and reduce longevity risk.
jong.kim: ugh. are those org-scoped keys or per-project? any labels we can use to bulk target?
amanda.lee: org-scoped. no consistent labels. some are baked into k8s secrets, some in legacy deploy scripts.
karim.nasser: quick thought: we should differentiate 'long-lived credential *store*' vs 'service session token'. propose: keep a short-lived session token for most service-to-service and offer a backfill path for long-lived keys that are allowed but flagged and tracked.
maria.garcia: +1. also need to consider audit/logging — rotating keys breaks attribution if we don't stitch sessions to identities.
amanda.lee: exactly — session stitching is the hard part. how do we do handoff with minimal disruption? we can't revoke everything at once.
jong.kim: phased approach: 1) inventory and tag keys 2) issue temporary exchange token via auth-broker for flagged clients 3) enforce TTL and rotate 4) revoke old keys after grace window.
karim.nasser: agree. tradeoffs: broker adds latency and complexity; client updates needed. but it centralizes migration logic and lets us add PoP later.
maria.garcia: what about having a 'compat-mode' on endpoints — accept both old API key format and Exchange tokens for 90d while logging both, then error for org-admin created keys after 90d?
amanda.lee: compat-mode seems sensible. we should add an opt-in header so newer SDKs can `Prefer: token-exchange` and avoid falling back.
jong.kim: SDK work: add transparent exchange flow: if you detect a long-lived key in env, do a one-time exchange to ephemeral token, cache it with TTL, then refresh. minimal code change in apps.
karim.nasser: security-wise I want proof-of-possession (PoP) for exchanged tokens to prevent token-theft replay from leaked secrets. but PoP adds client crypto work. is that required now or later?
maria.garcia: prioritize rotation + PoP as optional. roadmap: rotate & attach short-lived sessions now, plan PoP in next quarter for high-risk clients.
amanda.lee: specifics: inventory script + k8s scanner, mark keys 'legacy' in metadata store. infra-team to run scanner and emit report.
jong.kim: infra-bot: scheduled scanner job created? infra-bot: scheduled job "legacy-key-scan" created. cron: 0 3 * * 1. output goes to #eng-security/reports.
amanda.lee: nice. next: auth-broker design notes — minimal MVP should support: POST /exchange { api_key } -> { access_token, expires_in, client_id }
amanda.lee: and token introspect endpoint for internal services to validate quickly.
karim.nasser: add a rate-limit & quota check during exchange to avoid abuse. also log request origin IP + k8s pod identity for trace.
maria.garcia: audit logs must include original api_key id (hashed), new token id, and principal mapping. retention policy: 1y for incidents, 7d for routine.
jong.kim: migration window proposal: 90 days phased: 30d inventory & opt-in SDK push, 30d exchange + compat-mode, 30d strict enforcement + revoke.
amanda.lee: contingency: add canary revocation policy: choose a low-risk org and run full rotate there; measure errors and latencies.
karim.nasser: operational considerations: token cache TTL on clients should be shorter than server TTL by a buffer to avoid stale reuse. also need graceful 401->refresh paths.
maria.garcia: one more: RBAC mapping. When exchanging, we need to map the legacy org-level key to the current RBAC roles. If unclear, default to least-privilege read-only and require explicit roll-up for write perms.
amanda.lee: that could break some jobs — include an "assert-roles" endpoint so owners can claim higher roles and prove via a small challenge (owner email + oauth).
jong.kim: implementation tasks: 1) scanner + report (infra) 2) auth-broker prototype + exchange endpoint (eng-auth) 3) SDK transparent exchange (devx) 4) audit retention & logs (security) 5) rollout plan + canary (product/ops)
karim.nasser: compatibility note: some internal services still embed keys in binary images. for those, we'll need a build-time rewrap plugin that exchanges at deploy-time and writes ephemeral to pod secrets.
maria.garcia: add to migration checklist: identify binaries, update CI, add rewrap step in deploy pipeline.
amanda.lee: great. final question: do we sunset org-scoped keys entirely or keep them for service accounts with strict policy?
karim.nasser: keep them for managed service-accounts but require they be created by an admin and have short explicit rotation windows (<= 180d) + PoP for high privilege.
jong.kim: +1. docs & billing note: inform customers of potential disruptions and provide migration tooling.
amanda.lee: I'll draft an RFC summarizing: inventory tooling, broker MVP, SDK changes, rollout timeline, RBAC fallback rules, and risk mitigation. aim to publish tomorrow.
maria.garcia: thanks — ping me on the draft for audit wording.
amanda.lee: will do. :thumbsup:
